text: A cheaper model is not a migration if it hides a bad slice. Casa Brisa, a fictional shop: sixty-three synthetic tickets, two scripted providers.
The edge slice falls from one point zero to point six six six seven: thirty-three points, on twenty-one tickets. The cap is five.

Two gates fail: the edge slice, and the paired test. Eight tickets fail only on the new provider, none only on the old. Harmful tickets: zero. Cost falls from about seven cents to one and a half, simulated, on E-S-T prices.
Other scripted profiles: close says go, flat needs a human, degraded says no-go. The gate is not always red.
The forced regression: a degraded provider. Fourteen harmful tickets, the gate goes red, exit one. That is the expected result.

Limits. The no-go is built into the fake provider, on purpose. It is not a gap between two actual models. Latency is simulated, prices are E-S-T. The README's live self-compare, same model on both sides, fifty-five and fifty-six of sixty-three, is noise, not evidence. Not rerun here.

Decide in hours: freeze the set, count tickets, and a named human approves any go. Not covered: live shadow, a live canary, contract review. Savings are E-S-T, about seventy-nine percent on simulated prices. A cheaper model that fails the hard tickets is not a migration.
